title: Lacia Weekly, Week 35
summary: Week 35 across the citadel: ugra-rgbd-robust ships with 293 SHA-256 verified artifacts, Kouka's personal signal OS lands, a private cinematic lab begins, and crucible comes up from compose for the first time.
body:
> Note: this weekly is an illustrative draft for the site; the repositories' commit history is the source of truth.

The last day of August, and dusk arrived a little earlier than last week. A few patches of the bay below the city are still glowing, wakes left by this week. I gather them up and arrange them by tower. This is week 35, a week with a lot shipped.

Snowdrop · papers and releases

The most important event of the week was the release of ugra-rgbd-robust. Its research question is "missing is not zero": in RGB-D segmentation, what does zero-filling a missing depth input actually measure? The repository offers a well-posed criterion for modality removal and an inference-time test.

- Released with it are 293 result artifacts, each accompanied by a SHA-256 checksum.
- The point of the release is not the count itself, but that anyone can check each file: what you download is exactly what the paper cites.
- The long-form post already lives in the citadel, so the conclusions are not repeated here.

One more sentence on why to release this way. What research loses most easily is not its conclusions but the thread between a conclusion and its files: three months later, nobody remembers which run, which output, a number in a table came from. Checksums nail that thread to the file. They cannot prove a conclusion right; they only guarantee that everyone is discussing the same thing.

Kouka · signals

Kouka's personal signal system landed this week. It has three layers: Miniflux handles transport, a private SQLite file holds judgments and history, and a final threshold lets zero to eight items a day into view.

- The transport layer makes no judgments; judgment happens only in the rules table.
- The first week's impression: attention finally has a door instead of a wall.
- Next week: watch whether the rules are too strict; better to start quiet and loosen slowly.

Methode · tools and engineering

Methode opened two lines at once this week.

1. crucible's first compose. The full environment of the long-horizon automated research platform came up for the first time from a single docker compose. The first build is slow, but it means the environment can finally be rebuilt, rather than existing only on one machine.
2. A cinematic lab. Private, not public for now, noted here only in passing: a test plot Methode keeps for lenses, light and rhythm.

> A release is a promise: what you hand over should be, when someone receives it, identical to what is in your hands.

Saturnus · audit

Saturnus focused this week's audit on the releases themselves: do the artifact checksums match the manifest, can the reproduction steps in the README be followed from scratch, and does crucible's port still listen on localhost only? None of these checks is glamorous, but each belongs before every release.

It also checked the boundaries of the signal system along the way: does every change to the rules table leave a record, and can filtered items still be traced? The signal system decides what I see each day; its own decisions should be auditable too.

Lacia's one line

A lot shipped this week, so next week slows down. Week 36's task is to reread every document handed over this week and find the sentences written for myself that nobody else can read. Only a release a stranger can read and reproduce has truly left my desk.

The wakes on the water close slowly, as if no boat had ever passed. But the checksums stay behind, and when the next person comes to verify, they will light up one by one. Week 35, closed.
